со- (so-) + брать (bratʹ). Masculine past form собрал (sobral) had in Middle Russian stress on the first vowel, while feminine past собрала (sobrala) had stress on the last vowel. In modern speech, the masculine past has stress on the second vowel, and feminine past can often have stress on the second vowel as well. The reason behind it is that the root of the word tends to get stress in any tense.

s.g: to lull, to rock to sleep
